electricalCircuitBasics.title: Basic Lamp Circuit
electricalCircuitBasics.description: How a car lamp circuit works and how to diagnose faults with a Power Probe.
electricalCircuitBasics.section1Subtitle: Click the switch to activate the circuit. Click each component to see its description.
electricalCircuitBasics.section2Subtitle: Select each fault type to see how it affects the circuit.
electricalCircuitBasics.section3Subtitle: Step-by-step procedure to locate circuit faults.
electricalCircuitBasics.section4Subtitle: 3 diagnostic questions. Select the best answer for each.
electricalCircuitBasics.quickQuestion: 🤔 Quick question: What happens if the fuse blows?
electricalCircuitBasics.fuseExplanation: When the fuse blows, its internal filament breaks and creates an opening in the circuit. This stops current flow completely — the lamp receives no voltage and goes off.
electricalCircuitBasics.diagTipContent: Always start by testing the power source (battery). If the source is good, test each component sequentially toward the load. The point where voltage disappears is where the fault is.

battery.label: 🔋 Battery (12V)
battery.desc: The battery is the energy source of the circuit. It provides 12 volts of direct current (DC). Without a battery there is no circuit.

fuse.label: ⚡ Fuse
fuse.desc: The fuse protects the circuit against overloads. If the current exceeds the fuse's amperage, the filament breaks and the circuit opens — protecting the other components.

switch.label: 🔀 Switch
switch.desc: The switch controls current flow. In the OPEN position it interrupts the circuit (lamp off). In the CLOSED position it completes the circuit (lamp on).

lamp.label: 💡 Lamp
lamp.desc: The lamp is the circuit load. It converts electrical energy into light and heat. If the lamp does not turn on, the issue could be the lamp itself or any component before it.

ground.label: ⏚ Ground
ground.desc: The ground completes the circuit back to the battery. Without a good ground connection, the circuit does not work even if all other components are good.

fuses.q1b: The circuit opens and the lamp goes off

normal.label: ✅ Normal
normal.title: Normal Circuit
normal.desc: All components working correctly. Voltage flows from battery through fuse, switch and lamp to ground. Lamp turns on.

open.label: 🔴 Open Circuit
open.title: Open Circuit
open.desc: A break in the circuit prevents current flow. Can be a blown fuse, broken wire, defective switch or bad ground. Lamp does not turn on.

short.label: ⚠️ Short Circuit
short.title: Short Circuit
short.desc: A wire or component creates an unintended path to ground before reaching the load. This causes excessive current that blows the fuse. This is the most dangerous fault type.

resistance.label: 🟡 High Resistance
resistance.title: High Resistance
resistance.desc: A corroded connection, corroded terminal or damaged wire creates extra resistance. The lamp turns on but dimly. Over time it can cause overheating and complete failure.
resistance.reading: Voltage drop at the high-resistance point (e.g. 9V at lamp instead of 12V)

probe.step1Desc: Connect the RED wire of the Power Probe to the POSITIVE (+) battery terminal. Connect the BLACK wire to the NEGATIVE (−) terminal or chassis ground.
probe.step1Tip: The Power Probe always needs a direct battery reference to work correctly.
probe.step2Desc: Touch the Power Probe tip to the positive (+) battery terminal. You should see 12V and the GREEN light turn on.
probe.step2Tip: If you don't see 12V here, the problem is the battery. Charge or replace it.
probe.step3Desc: Touch the fuse output (load side). If the fuse is good, you should see 12V. If you see 0V, the fuse is blown.
probe.step3Tip: You can test both sides of the fuse. If the input side has voltage but the output doesn't, the fuse is blown.
probe.step4Desc: Touch the switch input terminal (the one coming from the fuse). You should see 12V here regardless of whether the switch is open or closed.
probe.step4Tip: If there is no voltage at the switch input, the problem is before it — check the fuse and wires.
probe.step5Desc: With the switch in the ON position, touch its output terminal. If the switch works correctly, you should see 12V. If you see 0V with the switch ON, the switch is defective.
probe.step5Tip: This is the key diagnosis: 12V input + 0V output with switch ON = bad switch. Replace the switch!
probe.step6Desc: Touch the lamp's ground connection with the Power Probe. If the Power Probe shows a ground signal, the ground is good.
probe.step6Tip: A bad ground can cause the lamp to turn on dimly or not at all, even if it has voltage at the input.

quiz.q1: What does the Power Probe show when there is an open circuit on the load side?
quiz.q1exp: In an open circuit, current cannot flow. The Power Probe will not detect voltage on the load side (after the break point). Before the break point it will still show 12V.
quiz.q2: Where should you connect the BLACK (negative) wire of the Power Probe for accurate readings?
quiz.q2a: To any metal part of the vehicle
quiz.q2b: To the battery negative terminal or a verified chassis ground
quiz.q2d: It doesn't matter — the Power Probe self-calibrates
quiz.q2exp: The ground reference must be solid and direct. A bad ground will give incorrect readings. Always use the battery negative terminal or a verified chassis ground point.
quiz.q3: You have 12V at the switch input but 0V at its output with the switch in the ON position. What is the problem?
quiz.q3exp: 12V at the input and 0V at the output with the switch ON is the definitive diagnosis of a defective switch. The component that has voltage at its input but does not pass it to its output is the failed component.
